Yes, the appellate court will likely reverse. Compliance with zoning and building codes is not a complete defense to a private nuisance claim, and the owner showed that a different placement would avoid the interference, so the trial court's "build anywhere the codes allow" rule is the wrong test. The result depends on the jurisdiction: a court following the traditional no-right-to-light rule (*Fontainebleau*) could still affirm, but a court that recognizes solar-obstruction nuisance (*Prah v. Maretti*) or has a solar access statute would likely reverse.

CONFIDENCE: 70
